title: Area and Perimeter (KS2)
subject: Maths
strapline: The distance around a shape and the space inside it.
facts: Perimeter is the total distance all the way around the outside of a shape.
To find a perimeter, add up the lengths of all the sides.
Area is the amount of flat space inside a shape, measured in square units (cm², m²).
Area of a rectangle = length × width.
Perimeter is measured in units of length (cm, m); area is measured in square units (cm², m²).
Two shapes can have the same area but a different perimeter, and vice versa.
For an L-shape, split it into rectangles, find each area, then add them.

quick_quiz.q: A rectangle is 5cm by 3cm. What is its area?
What is the perimeter of a 5cm by 3cm rectangle?
Which is measured in cm²: area or perimeter?

teacher_tips: Count squares for area first, then generalise to length × width.
Keep the units distinct: cm for perimeter, cm² for area.
Use compound (L-shaped) problems to stretch confident children.
